Later we will modify this commutativity constraint by a sign to make sure that the functor $\mathsf{F}$ sends it to the standard commutativity constraint on vector spaces; see §8.2.

2.

One may note here that the twisted product
$\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\widetilde{\times}\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ , while playing a key role in the proof, is
not involved in the definition of the fusion product, since the maps
$i$ and $j$ only deal with the Beĭlinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ and
$\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$ . The two points $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ , which are not
interchangeable in the definition of $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\widetilde{\times}\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ ,
play the same role in $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$ . This property is the basis for the
construction of the commutativity constraint.

3.

One can describe the associativity constraint considered in §6.4 also in terms of the fusion procedure, using the Beĭlinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{3}}$ over $X^{3}$ .

8 Further study of the fiber functor

8.1 Compatibility of $\mathsf{F}$ with the convolution product

In Sections 6–7
we have endowed our category $\mathrm{P}_{G_{\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ with a convolution
product $\star$ , defined either in the “easy” way with the convolution diagram (6.2)
or with the fusion procedure. The latter even allows to define a
commutativity constraint. We now want to show that the functor

$\mathsf{F}=\mathsf{H}^{\bullet}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\bm{?}):\mathrm{P}_{G_{\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$

is a fiber functor in the sense of Remark 2.8(2); in other words that this is an exact and faithful functor
that maps the convolution product of sheaves to the tensor product of
vector spaces while respecting the associativity, the unit, and the
commutativity constraints of these categories.

The exactness and the faithfulness of $\mathsf{F}$ have already been
proved in Theorem 5.9(2).

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
